subject: Intermittent token latency & 5xx spikes — prefix cache routing suspected
messages:
From: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@acmeai.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: support@acmeai.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency & 5xx spike on prod (region us-west)

Hi Karthik,

Over the past two hours we've seen token latency jump from ~45ms to >450ms and an increase in 5xx errors for our inference route r-acme-embed-prod. Throughput dropped despite steady incoming QPS. We attached logs and a p95/p99 dashboard snapshot.

This is impacting our LLM-based scoring pipeline; we had to pause processing to avoid bad downstream decisions. Can you triage and confirm whether this is a config problem on your side (we didn't change anything)?

Thanks,
Olivia Reed
Head of ML Ops, Acme AI

On Sat, May 30, 2026 at 5:28 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the heads-up, Olivia — sorry you're seeing this. I'm escalating to our infra on-call and looping in Marcus from runtime. We'll treat this as a Sev-1 until resolved.

Quick findings from initial triage:
- Host metrics show heavy queue lengths on a subset of GPU workers servicing r-acme-embed-prod during the window Olivia reported.
- Per-prefix cache occupancy spikes correlate with those workers — a narrow set of prefixes (user/session prefixes used by Acme) are getting disproportionate cache entries.
- Batching telemetry shows unusually large in-flight batches combined with long wait times for the first token (head-of-line blocking).
- Error traces point to timeout-to-retry cascades when a leader batch gets stalled.

Hypothesis: a misrouted prefix-caching policy caused prefix entries to be pinned to a small worker shard; batching windows then caused HOL blocking under load, amplifying latency and triggering transient 5xx as retries stacked. This is not classical memory thrash; it's more of a routing/pinning + batching interaction.

Immediate mitigation plan (executing now):
1) Temporarily widen the prefix shard mapping (redistribute pinned prefixes across more workers) — will reduce hot partitions.
2) Reduce per-request batch wait window from 12ms to 4ms for the affected route to lower HOL exposure.
3) Enable aggressive KV cache eviction for prefixes flagged as hot for 10 minutes to break any bad stuck state.

I'll post logs and a patch id when changes are live.

-Marcus Lin
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@acmeai.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Action update: prefix redistribution and batch window reduced

Hi Olivia — quick update on actions we deployed at 18:02 PST: 
- Prefix shard mapping widened (patch id: rth-20260530-209). Cache entries for the 12 identified hot prefixes are now spread across 6 additional workers.
- Batch wait window for r-acme-embed-prod reduced from 12ms -> 4ms.
- Temporary aggressive eviction policy enabled for flagged prefixes (10 min TTL).

Early results: p95 latency dropped from ~450ms to ~75ms within 3 minutes; error-rate (5xx) down to baseline. We're keeping the mitigation in place and collecting telemetry for 2 hours.

Actions next 24h:
- Run a replay across your sample traces to ensure no request-level correctness regressions.
- We'll instrument per-prefix queue occupancy and head-of-line duration in the dashboard (ETA: 6 hours).
- Plan a config fix to prevent future pinning misroutes (post-mortem + automated validation).

Please let us know if you still see anomalies.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com

Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: mitigation notes, SLA impact, and next steps

Hi Olivia — following up with the requested details. Forwarding the playbook we used and a short assessment of SLA impact.

Playbook summary (executed):
- Identify hot prefixes via telemetry query (queries: prefix_occupancy > 80% over 30s).
- Widen shard mapping and trigger rebalance (patch rth-20260530-209).
- Temporarily reduce batch window to 4ms for r-acme-embed-prod.
- Enable aggressive eviction for hot prefixes for 10 minutes.
- Monitor p50/p95/p99 and 5xx counts for 30 minutes; rollback if errors increase.

SLA and cost note: reducing the batch wait window will generally increase per-token compute cost because batching efficiency drops. If we keep the 4ms window permanently it may increase your unit cost by ~3-6% depending on traffic mix. That said, the proper long-term fix is to prevent prefix pinning via routing policy verification and more dynamic shard balancing, which preserves batching efficiency.

Proposed next steps:
- Engineering to produce a config patch preventing pinning misroutes and add a unit test for prefix-to-shard hashing (owner: Marcus, ETA: 4 days).
- Add per-prefix HOL metrics and an alert (owner: Observability team, ETA: 6 hours to dashboard, ETA: 2d to alert rule).
- Offer one incident credit equivalent to 24h of baseline usage for the affected service while we complete the patch (commercial team to confirm).

I'll open a follow-up doc in our shared drive with detailed logs and the runbook steps. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/acmeai/diagnostics/20260530

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min postmortem with Engineering and your ML Ops next week.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
